problems.title: One instruction, many FMAs
problems.solution: 4,096 FMAs, the work of 128 warp FMA instructions.

problems.title: GW-1 tensor peak
problems.statement: 256 FMAs per SM per cycle, 16 SMs, 1.5 GHz.

problems.title: An FP16 accumulator
problems.statement: Add 1.0 to an FP16 accumulator 4,096 times, starting from 0, rounding after each add.
problems.solution: (a) 2048: once the accumulator reaches 2,048, adding 1 rounds back down (ties to even). (b) $2^{11-10} = 2$. Hence FP32 accumulation in every tensor-core GEMM.

problems.title: Rounding steps
problems.statement: Relative rounding (unit roundoff) of each input format.
problems.solution: $4.9 \times 10^{-4}$, $3.9 \times 10^{-3}$ and $0.0625$. FP8 changes inputs by up to 6%, which is why it needs per-tensor (or per-block) scaling.

problems.title: An error budget
problems.statement: FP16 inputs, FP32 accumulation, n = 1024, all entries in [−1, 1].

parts.prompt: A typical (random-walk) error is about $\sqrt{n}$ times one term's error. Estimate it.

hints: Each product carries up to $2 \cdot 2^{-11}$ relative error.
problems.solution: (a) 1.0 in the worst case. (b) About $32 \times 0.001 = 0.03$. A test with absolute tolerance 1e-3 will fail; the right tolerance comes from the budget, scaled to the data.

problems.title: Fragments
problems.statement: The simulator's accumulator layout: lane ℓ holds row ℓ ≫ 1, columns (ℓ & 1)·8 to +7.
hints: Row r is held by lanes 2r and 2r + 1.
problems.solution: (a) 13 ≫ 1 = 6. (b) 13 is odd: columns 8–15. (c) Row 9 → lanes 18 and 19; column 3 < 8 → lane 18.

problems.title: Memory-bound again
problems.statement: Tensor cores at 12,288 GFLOP/s on the GW-1 (512 GB/s). A 64 × 64-tiled kernel has DRAM intensity about 16.
problems.solution: Ridge 24, attainable 8,192 GFLOP/s: memory-bound. The kernel that was comfortably compute-bound in FP32 now needs bigger tiles and deeper pipelines.

problems.title: FP16 inputs halve the bytes
problems.statement: The same tiled kernel with FP16 inputs (2 bytes) instead of FP32: intensity is about T/2 instead of T/4.

parts.prompt: Smallest power-of-two T above the tensor ridge of 24 with FP16 inputs?

problems.solution: (a) T > 48: 64. (b) T > 24: 32. Narrower inputs raise intensity as well as math rate, which is half of why low precision is so effective.

problems.title: Range

parts.prompt: BF16's largest finite value is about…
Which training setup needs loss scaling?

problems.solution: BF16 has FP32's range, so gradients don't underflow. FP16's narrow range makes small gradients flush to zero unless the loss is scaled up first (the Mixed Precision Training paper).

problems.title: Which formats have FP32's range?
problems.solution: FP32, TF32 and BF16. TF32 is "FP32 range, FP16 precision", which is why "FP32" GEMMs on Ampere tensor cores lose precision silently unless you opt out.
